title: Implant plugins uploaded through stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys

indicators.label: probe
indicators.note: Key test; the command log records it as not understood for a probe hostname. The attack tool names the UDRPC library with no library version and no vendor URL, while the owner's own dashboard has been seen sending a versioned library name followed by the vendor's URL

indicators.label: command
indicators.note: An upload-plugin command and its reply, observed across four sites; a reply the size of the ordinary front page means nothing reached a handler
Description line of the implant template's plugin header; a variant with a new description evades it
Author line of the implant template's plugin header
Constant name in the published analysis of the template
Constant name in the published analysis of the template
Two or three plain words plus an optional short hex or digit suffix; most legitimate slugs match too, so it counts only beside a headerless plugin or a strong hit
Implant trigger token, written at activation and left behind when the folder is quarantined; confirm no installed plugin owns the prefix
Written at activation beside the sync token
The working build's install timestamp; common in legitimate plugins, so a finding only when its prefix is the slug of a plugin missing from disk
The working build's daily hook; WP-Cron keeps rescheduling it after the folder is gone
Login pattern the implant creates; no such user was ever created on the sites studied
Login pattern from the published analysis
The implant's user gets a placeholder address; sites also give byline accounts placeholder addresses, so check the role and the registration date
Stored connection keys; on a site with a key, the key itself is the exposure, and reinstalling or updating UpdraftPlus while it is stored revives it
The last 50 remote commands with time, address and user agent; decode it from the verified dump before any cleanup deletes UpdraftPlus's options
UDRPC's replay cache; its value holds the time of the last command
